t: Matrix Block Sum — Prefix Sum (2D) Editorial
o: For each cell $(i,j)$ we must output the sum of all matrix values inside the square window of radius $k$ centered at that cell, clipped to the matrix bounds. In Example 1 ($k=1$), `answer[0][0]` covers rows 0–1 and cols 0–1: $1+2+4+5=12$. In Example 2 ($k=2$), every window spans the whole $3\times3$ matrix, so all answers equal 45. With $m,n \le 100$, even a brute force over each window is at most $100^2 \times 200^2 = 4\times10^8$ operations — borderline, so a prefix-sum approach giving $O(mn)$ is clearly preferable.
k: A 2D prefix sum array P where P[i][j] = sum of mat[0..i-1][0..j-1] lets any rectangle sum be computed in O(1) via inclusion-exclusion.
Clipping the window to valid bounds is just clamping row range to [max(0,i-k), min(m-1,i+k)] and similarly for columns.
Building the answer costs O(mn) total since each cell's block sum is a constant-time rectangle query.

a.i: For every cell, directly loop over all positions in its clipped window and accumulate the sum. This mirrors the problem statement exactly and works within constraints because windows are at most $201\times201$ and the grid is small. It needs no extra data structures beyond the answer matrix.
s: For each cell (i, j), compute r1=max(0,i-k), r2=min(m-1,i+k), c1=max(0,j-k), c2=min(n-1,j+k).
Sum mat[r][c] over all r in [r1,r2] and c in [c1,c2].
Store the sum in answer[i][j] and return the matrix.
a.t: O(m·n·k²) — each of the m·n cells scans up to (2k+1)² entries.
a.sp: O(m·n) for the answer matrix only (or O(1) extra if allowed to overwrite input).

a.i: Build a padded prefix-sum matrix P of size $(m+1)\times(n+1)$ where $P[i][j]$ stores the sum of the rectangle from $(0,0)$ to $(i-1,j-1)$. Then the sum of any rectangle with corners $(r_1,c_1)$–$(r_2,c_2)$ inclusive equals $P[r_2+1][c_2+1] - P[r_1][c_2+1] - P[r_2+1][c_1] + P[r_1][c_1]$ by inclusion-exclusion. Each block sum becomes an $O(1)$ query after $O(mn)$ preprocessing.
s: Build P with dimensions (m+1) x (n+1), zeros in row 0 and column 0.
For each cell (i, j), set r1=max(0,i-k), r2=min(m-1,i+k), c1=max(0,j-k), c2=min(n-1,j+k).
a.t: O(m·n) — one pass to build the prefix sums plus one constant-time query per cell.
a.sp: O(m·n) for the prefix-sum table and the answer matrix.

w: In an interview, mention brute force briefly, then lead with the 2D prefix-sum solution — it demonstrates the standard inclusion-exclusion technique and hits optimal complexity. Common pitfalls: off-by-one errors between 0-indexed matrix coordinates and 1-indexed prefix array (hence the padding row/column of zeros), forgetting to clamp the window at borders, and sign mistakes in the four-term inclusion-exclusion formula. Edge cases: k ≥ max(m,n) makes every answer the total matrix sum; single-row or single-column matrices. Follow-ups may ask for streaming updates (use a 2D Binary Indexed Tree for point updates with range queries) or handling very large matrices where you'd avoid materializing the full prefix table.
